title: Evidence staging and exfiltration guardrails — staging node and SIEM-export controls
summary: Spec for an intermediate evidence staging layer and runtime guardrails to prevent accidental or malicious exfiltration during evidence harvest, plus RBAC and SIEM export controls. Focuses on staging node semantics, TTL/watermarking, signed manifests, export throttles and audit schema markers for downstream SIEM ingestion.
body:
Purpose:
This document defines the runtime contract and operational guardrails for evidence staging nodes (transient storage used by collectors and harvesters), with the explicit goal of minimizing accidental data exfiltration risk and improving downstream SIEM export hygiene. It complements collector design notes and audit ingestion pipelines by prescribing: role-scoped access, cryptographic manifests, TTL/watermarking rules, schema markers for exports, and an incident playbook for suspected exfiltration.

Scope and motivation:
- Applies to all collector processes and staging nodes under the security-and-compliance shared drive and associated cloud accounts (managed by Evidence Orchestrator).
- Not a replacement for centralized SIEM policies; intended to be a pre-export shield that enforces minimal-resolution, redaction, and export-limits.
- Addresses observed gaps: large raw evidence snapshots staging undetected, ad-hoc exports by devs with elevated keys, and lack of cryptographic linkage between staging content and exported packages.

Key goals (must-haves):
- Staging nodes must enforce per-tenant and per-collector RBAC.
- Every staged artifact must have a signed manifest: producer identity, schema version, field-level sensitivity tags, TTL, and a hash chain.
- Exports to SIEM or third-party sinks must be rate-limited and require an export token with narrow scope and time-bound validity.
- Automated detectors run on staging content to flag likely PII or secret material before export.
- Full audit trail preserved in the internal audit log with an export-proof marker anchored to the manifest.

Architecture overview (high level):
- Collectors -> Staging Node(s) (encrypted at rest) -> Export Gate -> SIEM / Archive
- Staging nodes are short-lived blob stores (S3-style) with enforced lifecycle policies.
- Export Gate is a microservice that validates manifests, runs export policies, communicates with RBAC service, and emits structured audit events.

Staging node semantics and lifecycle:
- Artifact write flow: collector writes artifact + unsigned metadata -> staging node assigns artifact-id and appends server-side metadata -> staging node returns a pre-auth manifest placeholder.
- Collector must submit a signed manifest within 30m of artifact creation. Missing manifest triggers quarantined cleanup.
- TTL policy: default 72 hours for transient evidence; for customer-sensitive artifacts TTL is configurable but has a 30-day max.
- Watermarking: each staging node maintains a monotonic watermark for exported sequences. Exports must only include items with watermark >= last-export-watermark to avoid reorder-based replay.
- Quarantine rules: artifacts with failed manifest validation, or those flagged by detectors, move to quarantine prefix and require explicit triage by a role with Quarantine-Triage permission.

Manifest spec (fields to include in every signed manifest):
- artifact_id: staging-node assigned id (string)
- producer: collector service id (string)
- produced_at: ISO8601 timestamp (string)
- schema_version: evidence-audit-schema vX.Y (string)
- sensitivity_tags: list of short tags like PHI, PII, CRED, INTERNAL (list of strings)
- field_summary: short free-text summary of fields (string)
- content_hash: SHA256 hex (string)
- prev_hash: optional chain pointer for grouped uploads (string)
- ttl_seconds: numeric string representing seconds (string)
- export_policy: short policy id controlling allowed sinks (string)
- signature: base64-ed signed blob (string)
Note: The manifest must be signed with the collector's private key (short-lived keys preferred).

RBAC model for staging and exports:
- Roles: collector-writer, collector-reader, triage-analyst, export-approver, admin-audit.
- Permissions: write-artifact, submit-manifest, read-artifact, read-quarantine, approve-export, revoke-export-token, view-audit-events.
- Principle of least privilege: collectors run as collector-writer but cannot approve exports. Export-approver is required for any export that includes sensitivity_tags beyond INTERNAL or for payloads larger than 10 MB.
- Role binding examples: service-account:collector-legacy -> collector-writer; user:Rina -> triage-analyst + view-audit-events.

Export Gate: validation and throttle behavior:
- Pre-checks (required) before export permit: manifest present and signature valid; content_hash matches blob; TTL not expired; export token valid and not previously consumed.
- Policy checks: consult export_policy in manifest and central policy store. Certain sinks (external SIEMs) may require additional redaction or field removal.
- Throttles: per-tenant export rate = baseline 50 exports/min by default, adaptive based on anomaly scores. Large-volume exports must be scheduled and require export-approver approval.
- Audit stamping: every export event writes a structured audit event with fields: export_id, artifact_ids[], producer, approver (if any), sink, watermark_before, watermark_after, export_hash, policy_id. These fields map to the company audit schema (see mapping below).

Detection and pre-export checks (automated):
- PII/secret detector: lightweight ML binary that returns scores (0-1) for categories (PII, secrets, credentials). Triggers: PII>0.85 or secrets>0.7.
- Size-based trigger: >10MB -> approve path.
- Frequency trigger: if same producer exports N artifacts in M minutes above historic baseline, throttle and alert.
- Redaction scanner: attempts structured field-level redaction for JSON-like artifacts (removes or masks fields tagged as CRED or SSN).

Audit log mapping (minimal example) -> capture these fields for SIEM export schema v2.3:
- event.kind: "evidence_export"
- event.time: ISO8601 UTC
- actor.id: producer id or approver id
- actor.role: role name
- target.ids: comma-separated artifact ids
- evidence.sensitivity: comma-separated sensitivity tags
- evidence.schema_version: vX.Y
- export.sink: sink-id or URI
- export.size_bytes: numeric string
- export.hash: SHA256
- export.approval: "auto" | "manual"
- export.policy_id: policy id
- export.watermark_from: numeric string (watermark before)
- export.watermark_to: numeric string (watermark after)
- notes: free text short

Operational playbooks (short):
- Suspected exfiltration (automated detection flagged + manual confirmation):
  1) Immediately revoke export tokens (ExportGate API: revoke-export-token --tenant <t> --since <ts>).
  2) Put staging node into read-only mode; snapshot staging metadata for forensic analysis.
  3) Create forensic export (sealed archive) with chain-of-custody manifest and assign to triage-analyst.
  4) Notify security pager and start 4-hour incident timer for containment actions.
  5) If confirmed exfiltration, escalate to legal + CISO; retain artifacts for at least 1 year (per retention policy) but mark as sealed.

Engineering notes and implementation constraints:
- Staging nodes should be deployed in dedicated subnet with egress locked; only ExportGate has network path to SIEM endpoints.
- All signing keys for collectors are short-lived (max 24h) and rotate via KMS; collectors must support key-refresh without restart.
- ExportGate must implement idempotent export semantics (idempotency-key = export_id).
- For performance, detectors run on a subset sample for large batches; if sample detects risk, full-scan is required.

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- Existing collectors without manifests will be allowed to write to a compatibility prefix for 90 days, but their artifacts go to stricter TTL (24h) and must be manually approved for export.
- Provide a migration adapter library that signs manifests and injects sensitivity tags inferred from field names to minimize lift.

Open questions (to resolve before final sign-off):
- Sensitivity taxonomy — canonical list and mapping rules for ambiguous fields (e.g., device_id vs. mac_address).
- Export throttling defaults — what is the right baseline for high-throughput tenants?
- Triage SLAs for quarantine items — recommended 24h for low-severity, 4h for high-severity.

Appendix: quick sample manifest (human-readable):
artifact_id: stg-20251118-0001
producer: collector-pod-12
produced_at: 2025-11-18T14:22:31Z
schema_version: evidence-audit-schema v2.3
sensitivity_tags: [INTERNAL, PII]
field_summary: 'user-agent, ip, email-redact-candidate'
content_hash: 3f2b... (sha256)
prev_hash: null
ttl_seconds: 259200
export_policy: siem-low-sensitivity
signature: <base64-sig>

Notes and references:
- This spec should be implemented in the staging-node service and ExportGate proxy.
- Cross-reference: CONFLUENCE-SEC-EVID-482 (policy draft), JIRA-SCAN-9987 (detector work), github.com/redwood-inference/collector-plugins/pull/214 (migration adapter).
- For compliance: ensure retention and sealed-archive procedures meet legal retention hold requests.
